claim: The wapl-1(tm1814) deletion removes the first two exons of the C. elegans Wapl homolog.
source: In order to investigate the role of WAPL-1 during meiotic prophase, we used a deletion allele, wapl-1(tm1814), that removes the first two exons of the C. elegans Wapl homolog (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the gene structure and deletion.

claim: The WAPL-1 protein is absent in wapl-1(tm1814) mutants.
source: Western blot analysis on whole-worm protein extracts showed that the WAPL-1 protein is absent in wapl-1(tm1814) mutants, confirming that the tm1814 deletion is a null allele of wapl-1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1B demonstrates absence of WAPL-1 protein in the mutant.

claim: wapl-1(tm1814) is a null allele of wapl-1.
source: Western blot analysis on whole-worm protein extracts showed that the WAPL-1 protein is absent in wapl-1(tm1814) mutants, confirming that the tm1814 deletion is a null allele of wapl-1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The absence of WAPL-1 protein in the mutant confirms it is a null allele.

claim: Homozygous wapl-1(tm1814) mutants are viable.
source: Homozygous wapl-1(tm1814) mutants (referred from now on as wapl-1 mutants) are viable, but display a reduction in brood size and high levels of embryonic lethality (Figure 1C).
evidence: Direct observation and quantification of viable mutant worms.

claim: wapl-1 mutants display a reduction in brood size.
source: Homozygous wapl-1(tm1814) mutants (referred from now on as wapl-1 mutants) are viable, but display a reduction in brood size and high levels of embryonic lethality (Figure 1C).
evidence: Quantitative data in Figure 1C shows reduced brood size (142.7 for wapl-1 vs 228 for WT).

claim: wapl-1 mutants display high levels of embryonic lethality.
source: Homozygous wapl-1(tm1814) mutants (referred from now on as wapl-1 mutants) are viable, but display a reduction in brood size and high levels of embryonic lethality (Figure 1C).
evidence: Figure 1C shows 20.8% embryonic lethality in wapl-1 mutants compared to 0.26% in WT.

claim: wapl-1 mutants display somatic defects including high incidence of larval arrest.
source: In addition to these reproductive defects, wapl-1 mutants also displayed somatic defects, as demonstrated by the high incidence of larval arrest amongst the hatched wapl-1 embryos (Figure 1C) and by the presence of an egg laying defect in adult worms.
evidence: Figure 1C shows 28.38% larval arrest in wapl-1 mutants compared to 0.26% in WT.

claim: wapl-1 mutants display an egg laying defect in adult worms.
source: In addition to these reproductive defects, wapl-1 mutants also displayed somatic defects, as demonstrated by the high incidence of larval arrest amongst the hatched wapl-1 embryos (Figure 1C) and by the presence of an egg laying defect in adult worms.
evidence: Direct observation of adult worm phenotype.

claim: The overall organization of wapl-1 mutant germ lines appears largely normal with clearly defined mitotic and meiotic compartments.
source: The overall organization of wapl-1 mutant germ lines appears largely normal, with clearly defined mitotic and meiotic compartments in which the different stages of meiotic prophase can be easily identified (Figure 1D).
evidence: Visual comparison of DAPI-stained germ lines in Figure 1D shows similar organization between WT and wapl-1.

claim: Both wild type and wapl-1 mutant diakinesis oocytes display 6 DAPI-stained bodies.
source: In fact, observation of diakinesis oocytes (the last stage of meiotic prophase) showed that both wild type and wapl-1 mutant oocytes displayed 6 DAPI-stained bodies, demonstrating that WAPL-1 is not required for chiasma formation (Figure 1E).
evidence: Figure 1E shows microscopy images with 6 DAPI-stained bodies in both genotypes.

claim: WAPL-1 is not required for chiasma formation.
source: In fact, observation of diakinesis oocytes (the last stage of meiotic prophase) showed that both wild type and wapl-1 mutant oocytes displayed 6 DAPI-stained bodies, demonstrating that WAPL-1 is not required for chiasma formation (Figure 1E).
evidence: The presence of 6 DAPI-stained bodies (bivalents) indicates normal chiasma formation.

claim: A GFP::WAPL-1 transgene largely rescues the fertility defects of wapl-1(tm1814) mutants.
source: Expression of this transgene largely rescued the fertility defects of wapl-1(tm1814) mutants (Figure 1C), and western blot analysis confirmed the presence of a band of the expected molecular weight for the GFP::WAPL-1 fusion protein, although the overall intensity of this band was reduced compared to the endogenous WAPL-1 protein (Figure 1B).
evidence: Figure 1C shows improved brood size (179.8) and reduced embryonic lethality (3.26%) in wapl-1 mutants carrying the GFP::wapl-1 transgene.

claim: The GFP::WAPL-1 fusion protein is present in both mitotic and meiotic nuclei with a diffuse staining pattern.
source: Staining of germ lines from these transgenic worms with anti-GFP antibodies demonstrated that the GFP::WAPL-1 protein is present, with a diffuse staining pattern, in both mitotic and meiotic nuclei (Figure 1F).
evidence: Figure 1F shows GFP::WAPL-1 staining throughout the germ line.

claim: The intensity of GFP::WAPL-1 signal decreases drastically as transition zone nuclei acquire chromosome clustering characteristic of early meiotic prophase stages.
source: Interestingly, the intensity of the GFP::WAPL-1 signal decreased drastically as transition zone nuclei acquired the chromosome clustering characteristic of early meiotic prophase stages (leptotene and zygotene), peaking again at late pachytene and then remaining at similar high levels in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes (Figure 1F–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 show quantification of GFP::WAPL-1 intensity changes along the germ line.

claim: GFP::WAPL-1 intensity peaks again at late pachytene and remains at similar high levels in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes.
source: Interestingly, the intensity of the GFP::WAPL-1 signal decreased drastically as transition zone nuclei acquired the chromosome clustering characteristic of early meiotic prophase stages (leptotene and zygotene), peaking again at late pachytene and then remaining at similar high levels in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes (Figure 1F–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 show quantification of GFP::WAPL-1 intensity changes.

claim: RAD-51-positive recombination intermediates accumulate in mid pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants.
source: Despite this, RAD-51-positive recombination intermediates accumulate in mid pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants (Figure 2B).
evidence: Figure 2B shows increased RAD-51 foci in mid pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants compared to WT.

claim: RAD-51 foci are no longer detected in 98% of late pachytene nuclei of wild-type controls.
source: Furthermore, while RAD-51 foci were no longer detected in 98% of late pachytene nuclei of wild-type controls, 52% percent of nuclei in the same region of wapl-1 mutant germ lines displayed RAD-51 foci.
evidence: Quantification of RAD-51 foci in late pachytene nuclei.

claim: 52% of late pachytene nuclei in wapl-1 mutant germ lines display RAD-51 foci.
source: Furthermore, while RAD-51 foci were no longer detected in 98% of late pachytene nuclei of wild-type controls, 52% percent of nuclei in the same region of wapl-1 mutant germ lines displayed RAD-51 foci.
evidence: Quantification of RAD-51 foci in late pachytene nuclei.

claim: The repair of a subset of DSBs is delayed in wapl-1 mutants.
source: Thus, although crossover precursors are successfully formed, the repair of a subset of DSBs is delayed in wapl-1 mutants.
evidence: The persistence of RAD-51 foci in late pachytene indicates delayed DSB repair.

claim: Both wapl-1 mutants and WT controls display 6 COSA-1 foci per late pachytene nucleus.
source: We observed 6 COSA-1 and 6 ZHP-3 foci in both wapl-1 mutants and wild-type controls (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the normal presence of chiasmata in wapl-1 diakinesis oocytes.
evidence: Figure 2A shows quantification of COSA-1 foci with 6 foci per nucleus in both genotypes.

claim: Both wapl-1 mutants and WT controls display 6 ZHP-3 foci per late pachytene nucleus.
source: We observed 6 COSA-1 and 6 ZHP-3 foci in both wapl-1 mutants and wild-type controls (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the normal presence of chiasmata in wapl-1 diakinesis oocytes.
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 1 shows quantification of ZHP-3 foci with 6 foci per nucleus in both genotypes.

claim: All wapl-1 mutant embryos analyzed formed two polar bodies.
source: All wapl-1 mutant embryos analyzed formed two polar bodies, however, only 22% of post meiotic embryos (up to the two-cell embryo) displayed both polar bodies at the cortex, with most embryos (61%) displaying one polar body located away from the cortex and the remaining (11%) displaying both polar bodies away from the cortex (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Observation and quantification of polar body formation in fixed embryos.

claim: Only 22% of wapl-1 mutant post meiotic embryos display both polar bodies at the cortex.
source: All wapl-1 mutant embryos analyzed formed two polar bodies, however, only 22% of post meiotic embryos (up to the two-cell embryo) displayed both polar bodies at the cortex, with most embryos (61%) displaying one polar body located away from the cortex and the remaining (11%) displaying both polar bodies away from the cortex (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows quantification of polar body localization in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: 61% of wapl-1 mutant embryos display one polar body located away from the cortex.
source: All wapl-1 mutant embryos analyzed formed two polar bodies, however, only 22% of post meiotic embryos (up to the two-cell embryo) displayed both polar bodies at the cortex, with most embryos (61%) displaying one polar body located away from the cortex and the remaining (11%) displaying both polar bodies away from the cortex (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows quantification of polar body localization in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: 11% of wapl-1 mutant embryos display both polar bodies away from the cortex.
source: All wapl-1 mutant embryos analyzed formed two polar bodies, however, only 22% of post meiotic embryos (up to the two-cell embryo) displayed both polar bodies at the cortex, with most embryos (61%) displaying one polar body located away from the cortex and the remaining (11%) displaying both polar bodies away from the cortex (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Figure 3B shows quantification of polar body localization in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: Chromatin morphology in polar bodies is altered in wapl-1 mutants, often displaying separated DNA masses within the polar body.
source: In addition, we noticed that chromatin morphology in the polar bodies was altered in wapl-1 mutants, often displaying separated DNA masses within the polar body (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1 shows microscopy image of altered chromatin morphology in polar bodies.

claim: Most wapl-1 mutant embryos display defects in the extrusion of the second polar body.
source: To gain better understanding of the effect of WAPL-1 on polar body extrusion, we performed live imaging of the meiotic and early mitotic divisions in wild type and wapl-1 mutant embryos expressing histone H2B::mcherry (Figure 3D; Videos 1–3). These experiments confirmed that most wapl-1 mutant embryos display defects in the extrusion of the second polar body (Figure 3C–D; Videos 2–3).
evidence: Figure 3C shows quantification from live imaging: 7 out of 11 wapl-1 mutant embryos displayed defects.

claim: In 2 out of 11 wapl-1 mutant embryos, the second polar body underwent chromatin decondensation and condensation cycles mimicking changes in mitotic nuclei.
source: We also observed that in 2 out of 11 wapl-1 mutant embryos, the second polar body, which failed to migrate to the cortex, underwent chromatin decondesation and condensation cycles, mimicking the changes observed in the mitotic nuclei of the embryo (Figure 3D and Videos 2–3).
evidence: Direct observation from live imaging videos and Figure 3D.

claim: In 1 out of 11 filmed wapl-1 mutant embryos, the second polar body eventually fused with one of the mitotic nuclei generated after the first mitotic division.
source: Moreover, in 1 out of 11 filmed embryos the second polar body eventually fused with one of the mitotic nuclei generated after the first mitotic division (Figure 3D and Video 3), demonstrating that the failure in polar body extrusion of wapl-1 mutants can lead to aneuploidy in the embryo.
evidence: Direct observation from live imaging Video 3 and Figure 3D.

claim: The failure in polar body extrusion of wapl-1 mutants can lead to aneuploidy in the embryo.
source: Moreover, in 1 out of 11 filmed embryos the second polar body eventually fused with one of the mitotic nuclei generated after the first mitotic division (Figure 3D and Video 3), demonstrating that the failure in polar body extrusion of wapl-1 mutants can lead to aneuploidy in the embryo.
evidence: Fusion of polar body with mitotic nucleus would result in abnormal chromosome number.

claim: The oocyte pronucleus contains one single signal for the 5S rDNA in all embryos analyzed from wild-type (17) and wapl-1 mutants (17).
source: Labeling of the 5S rDNA locus on chromosome V in early embryos demonstrated that the oocyte pronucleus contained one single signal for the 5S rDNA in all embryos analyzed from wild-type (17) and wapl-1 mutants (17) (Figure 3E), suggesting that chromosome V segregates properly during the meiotic divisions in the absence of WAPL-1.
evidence: Figure 3E shows FISH analysis with single 5S rDNA signal in oocyte pronucleus.

claim: Chromosome V segregates properly during the meiotic divisions in the absence of WAPL-1.
source: Labeling of the 5S rDNA locus on chromosome V in early embryos demonstrated that the oocyte pronucleus contained one single signal for the 5S rDNA in all embryos analyzed from wild-type (17) and wapl-1 mutants (17) (Figure 3E), suggesting that chromosome V segregates properly during the meiotic divisions in the absence of WAPL-1.
evidence: The presence of a single 5S rDNA signal indicates proper chromosome V segregation.

claim: WAPL-1 is required to ensure proper polar body extrusion during the meiotic divisions.
source: This analysis demonstrates that WAPL-1 is required to ensure proper polar body extrusion during the meiotic divisions, and suggests that defects in this process may contribute to the embryonic lethality observed in wapl-1 mutants.
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence showing polar body extrusion defects in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: Defects in polar body extrusion may contribute to the embryonic lethality observed in wapl-1 mutants.
source: This analysis demonstrates that WAPL-1 is required to ensure proper polar body extrusion during the meiotic divisions, and suggests that defects in this process may contribute to the embryonic lethality observed in wapl-1 mutants.
evidence: Logical inference from observed polar body defects and embryonic lethality.

claim: Pachytene chromosomes in wapl-1 mutants appear more widely spaced within the nucleus and somewhat thicker than in wild-type controls.
source: During the initial observation of wapl-1 mutant germ lines we noticed that pachytene chromosomes appeared more widely spaced within the nucleus and somewhat thicker than in wild-type controls, suggesting that WAPL-1 may regulate the shape of meiotic chromosomes, as it does in mitotic cells (Tedeschi et al., 2013).
evidence: Direct observation of chromosome morphology in microscopy images.

claim: WAPL-1 may regulate the shape of meiotic chromosomes.
source: During the initial observation of wapl-1 mutant germ lines we noticed that pachytene chromosomes appeared more widely spaced within the nucleus and somewhat thicker than in wild-type controls, suggesting that WAPL-1 may regulate the shape of meiotic chromosomes, as it does in mitotic cells (Tedeschi et al., 2013).
evidence: Inference from observed chromosome morphology changes and comparison to mitotic cells.

claim: The overlap of HTP-3 tracks is reduced in wapl-1 mutants compared to wild-type.
source: Projections made from late pachytene nuclei of wild-type germ lines demonstrated ample overlap between different HTP-3-labeled axial elements, making it difficult to follow individual HTP-3 tracks along their whole length (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1). In contrast, the overlap of HTP-3 tracks was reduced in wapl-1 mutants, with some nuclei displaying six distinctive HTP-3 tracks (one per homolog pair) that could be clearly traced along their full length (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 4A shows visual comparison of HTP-3 staining patterns between WT and wapl-1.

claim: Some wapl-1 mutant nuclei display six distinctive HTP-3 tracks that can be clearly traced along their full length.
source: Projections made from late pachytene nuclei of wild-type germ lines demonstrated ample overlap between different HTP-3-labeled axial elements, making it difficult to follow individual HTP-3 tracks along their whole length (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1). In contrast, the overlap of HTP-3 tracks was reduced in wapl-1 mutants, with some nuclei displaying six distinctive HTP-3 tracks (one per homolog pair) that could be clearly traced along their full length (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 4A shows HTP-3 staining with six traceable tracks in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: There is a 28% decrease in axial element length in late pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants.
source: Measuring of total HTP-3 track length per nucleus demonstrated a 28% decrease in axial element length in late pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants (Figure 4B).
evidence: Figure 4B shows quantification of total HTP-3 length per nucleus.

claim: Late pachytene nuclei of syp-1 mutants display many long and thin HTP-3 tracks corresponding to individualized and elongated axial elements.
source: Late pachytene nuclei of syp-1 mutant germ lines displayed many long and thin HTP-3 tracks, corresponding to individualized and elongated axial elements (Figure 4C).
evidence: Figure 4C shows HTP-3 staining in syp-1 mutants.

claim: Late pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 syp-1 double mutants contain fewer HTP-3 tracks which appear bulkier than in syp-1 single mutants.
source: In contrast, late pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 syp-1 double mutants contained fewer HTP-3 tracks, which also appeared bulkier (Figure 4C).
evidence: Figure 4C shows visual comparison of HTP-3 staining between syp-1 and wapl-1 syp-1 mutants.

claim: The 5S rDNA locus is unpaired in most pachytene nuclei of both syp-1 and wapl-1 syp-1 double mutants.
source: Visualization of the 5S rDNA locus on chromosome V by FISH showed that this region was unpaired in most pachytene nuclei of both syp-1 and wapl-1 syp-1 double mutants, demonstrating that increased association of homologous axial elements is not responsible for the overall reduction in total axial element length observed in wapl-1 syp-1 mutants (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2 show FISH analysis of 5S rDNA pairing.

claim: Increased association of homologous axial elements is not responsible for the overall reduction in total axial element length observed in wapl-1 syp-1 mutants.
source: Visualization of the 5S rDNA locus on chromosome V by FISH showed that this region was unpaired in most pachytene nuclei of both syp-1 and wapl-1 syp-1 double mutants, demonstrating that increased association of homologous axial elements is not responsible for the overall reduction in total axial element length observed in wapl-1 syp-1 mutants (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: FISH data showing unpaired homologs rules out this mechanism.

claim: At late pachytene, each HIM-8 signal is associated with a short track of axial element in syp-1 wapl-1 double mutants.
source: Moreover, visualization of the X chromosome pairing center region using HIM-8 antibodies (Phillips et al., 2005) demonstrated that at late pachytene, when this region becomes separated in syp-1 mutants (MacQueen et al., 2002) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), each HIM-8 signal is associated with a short track of axial element in syp-1 wapl-1 double mutants (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Figure 4E shows HIM-8 and HTP-3 co-staining in syp-1 wapl-1 mutants.

claim: Removal of WAPL-1 induces dramatic changes in the overall organization of axial elements in pachytene nuclei.
source: Thus, removal of WAPL-1 induces dramatic changes in the overall organization of axial elements in pachytene nuclei.
evidence: Summary statement based on multiple observations of axial element changes.

claim: The appearance of elongated SMC-1::GFP structures (axial elements) coincides with the appearance of PLK-2 aggregates in wild-type germ lines.
source: In wild-type germ lines, the presence of elongated SMC-1::GFP structures (axial elements) coincided with the appearance of PLK-2 aggregates (8 out 8 germ lines), while nuclei preceding the formation of PLK-2 aggregates displayed diffuse SMC-1::GFP staining (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Figure 4F shows co-staining of SMC-1::GFP and PLK-2 in wild-type.

claim: Nuclei preceding the formation of PLK-2 aggregates display diffuse SMC-1::GFP staining in wild-type germ lines.
source: In wild-type germ lines, the presence of elongated SMC-1::GFP structures (axial elements) coincided with the appearance of PLK-2 aggregates (8 out 8 germ lines), while nuclei preceding the formation of PLK-2 aggregates displayed diffuse SMC-1::GFP staining (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Figure 4F shows diffuse SMC-1::GFP in pre-leptotene nuclei of wild-type.

claim: The appearance of elongated SMC-1::GFP structures precedes the formation of PLK-2 aggregates in transition zone nuclei of wapl-1 mutant germ lines.
source: In contrast, the appearance of elongated SMC-1::GFP structures preceded the formation of PLK-2 aggregates in transition zone nuclei of wapl-1 mutant germ lines (7 out of 8 germ lines, average of 5 nuclei per germ line) (Figure 4F).
evidence: Figure 4F shows SMC-1::GFP tracks in pre-leptotene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants.

claim: Transition zone nuclei in which chromosome clustering has not yet occurred display the highest intensity of WAPL-1 staining in the whole germ line.
source: Interestingly, transition zone nuclei in which chromosome clustering has not yet occurred display the highest intensity of WAPL-1 staining in the whole germ line (Figure 1F–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that high levels of WAPL-1 activity may be present in these nuclei.
evidence: Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 show GFP::WAPL-1 intensity quantification.

claim: High levels of WAPL-1 activity may be present in transition zone nuclei before chromosome clustering.
source: Interestingly, transition zone nuclei in which chromosome clustering has not yet occurred display the highest intensity of WAPL-1 staining in the whole germ line (Figure 1F–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that high levels of WAPL-1 activity may be present in these nuclei.
evidence: Inference from high GFP::WAPL-1 intensity in these nuclei.

claim: WAPL-1 regulates the timing of axial element assembly by antagonizing cohesin association with chromosomes during early meiosis.
source: These observations suggest that WAPL-1 regulates the timing of axial element assembly by antagonizing cohesin association with chromosomes during early meiosis.
evidence: Inference from premature appearance of SMC-1::GFP tracks in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: A diffuse pool of nuclear SMC-1::GFP starts accumulating in late pachytene, becoming very prominent in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes in wild-type germ lines.
source: Whether the early steps of this process involve major changes in the association of cohesin with chromosomes is not known, but imaging of SMC-1::GFP in wild-type germ lines demonstrated that a diffuse pool of nuclear SMC-1::GFP starts accumulating in late pachytene, becoming very prominent in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5 show SMC-1::GFP staining in late prophase.

claim: A diffuse pool of SMC-1::GFP is not observed in late prophase nuclei of wapl-1 mutants.
source: In contrast, a diffuse pool of SMC-1::GFP is not observed in late prophase nuclei of wapl-1 mutants (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 5 show lack of diffuse SMC-1::GFP in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: Axial elements remain as easily traceable linear structures in diplotene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants.
source: Moreover, while axial elements labeled by SMC-1::GFP remained as easily traceable linear structures in diplotene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants, they appeared as longer and more diffuse structures in wild-type oocytes (Figure 4G).
evidence: Figure 4G shows comparison of SMC-1::GFP-labeled axial elements in diplotene.

claim: Axial elements appear as longer and more diffuse structures in wild-type diplotene oocytes.
source: Moreover, while axial elements labeled by SMC-1::GFP remained as easily traceable linear structures in diplotene nuclei of wapl-1 mutants, they appeared as longer and more diffuse structures in wild-type oocytes (Figure 4G).
evidence: Figure 4G shows comparison of SMC-1::GFP-labeled axial elements in diplotene.

claim: WAPL-1 antagonizes cohesin binding during late pachytene and diplotene stages.
source: This suggests that WAPL-1 antagonizes cohesin binding during late pachytene and diplotene stages.
evidence: Inference from differences in SMC-1::GFP distribution between WT and wapl-1 mutants.

claim: The intensity of nuclear GFP::WAPL-1 undergoes an increase during late pachytene and diplotene compared with earlier prophase.
source: Interestingly, the intensity of nuclear GFP::WAPL-1 undergoes an increase during late pachytene and diplotene compared with earlier prophase (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that WAPL-1 activity may be increased during these stages.
evidence: Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 show GFP::WAPL-1 intensity quantification.

claim: WAPL-1 activity may be increased during late pachytene and diplotene stages.
source: Interestingly, the intensity of nuclear GFP::WAPL-1 undergoes an increase during late pachytene and diplotene compared with earlier prophase (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that WAPL-1 activity may be increased during these stages.
evidence: Inference from increased GFP::WAPL-1 intensity during these stages.

claim: Diplotene nuclei in wapl-1 mutants do not show the coiling of axial elements that is characteristic of this stage in wild-type germ lines.
source: In addition to the increased amount of cohesin associated with diplotene chromosomes, wapl-1 mutants display other defects in the chromosome remodeling process. First, diplotene nuclei in wapl-1 mutants do not show the coiling of axial elements that is characteristic of this stage in wild-type germ lines (Nabeshima et al., 2005) and instead axial elements visualized by SMC-1::GFP or anti-HTP-1 antibodies display a more linear appearance (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 6 show comparison of axial element morphology.

claim: Axial elements in wapl-1 mutant diplotene nuclei display a more linear appearance.
source: In addition to the increased amount of cohesin associated with diplotene chromosomes, wapl-1 mutants display other defects in the chromosome remodeling process. First, diplotene nuclei in wapl-1 mutants do not show the coiling of axial elements that is characteristic of this stage in wild-type germ lines (Nabeshima et al., 2005) and instead axial elements visualized by SMC-1::GFP or anti-HTP-1 antibodies display a more linear appearance (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 6 show axial element morphology in wapl-1 mutants.

claim: wapl-1 mutants display altered SC disassembly, as evidenced by the persistence of long tracks of SC component SYP-1 in diplotene oocytes.
source: Second, wapl-1 mutants display altered SC disassembly, as evidenced by the persistence of long tracks of SC component SYP-1 in diplotene oocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 6 shows SYP-1 staining in diplotene oocytes.

claim: Cohesin removal by WAPL-1 is an intrinsic feature of chromosome remodeling during late pachytene and diplotene.
source: These observations suggest that cohesin removal by WAPL-1 is an intrinsic feature of chromosome remodeling during late pachytene and diplotene.
evidence: Inference from multiple observations of cohesin changes during late prophase.

claim: wapl-1 mutants undergo meiotic prophase with increased levels of axis-associated cohesin.
source: The evidence presented above strongly suggests that wapl-1 mutants undergo meiotic prophase with increased levels of axis-associated cohesin.
evidence: Summary inference from multiple lines of evidence showing increased cohesin.

claim: The intensity of REC-8 staining appears very similar in wapl-1 mutant germ lines and wild-type controls.
source: Upon initial observation, the intensity of REC-8 staining appeared very similar in wapl-1 mutant germ lines and wild-type controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: Figure 5A shows visual comparison of REC-8 staining.

claim: The COH-3/4 signal is clearly increased in wapl-1 mutants.
source: However, the COH-3/4 signal was clearly increased in wapl-1 mutants (Figure 5A).
evidence: Figure 5A shows visual comparison of COH-3/4 staining.

claim: wapl-1 mutant germ lines display increased levels of COH-3/4 throughout meiotic prophase, with the highest differences detected in late pachytene nuclei.
source: A quantitative analysis of the mean nuclear intensity of REC-8 and COH-3/4 staining between leptotene and late pachytene confirmed that wapl-1 mutant germ lines display increased levels of COH-3/4 throughout meiotic prophase, with the highest differences detected in late pachytene nuclei (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B shows quantification of mean fluorescence intensity for REC-8 and COH-3/4.

claim: The average difference between axis-associated and inter-chromosomal signal for COH-3/4 is increased by 114% in wapl-1 mutants compared with wild-type controls.
source: The average difference between axis-associated and inter-chromosomal signal for COH-3/4 was increased by 114% in wapl-1 mutants compared with wild-type controls, while the increase observed for REC-8 and SMC-3 was 27% and 59% respectively (Figure 5C).
evidence: Figure 5C shows line profile quantification of cohesin intensity.

claim: The increase in axis-associated signal for REC-8 in wapl-1 mutants is 27% compared with wild-type controls.
source: The average difference between axis-associated and inter-chromosomal signal for COH-3/4 was increased by 114% in wapl-1 mutants compared with wild-type controls, while the increase observed for REC-8 and SMC-3 was 27% and 59% respectively (Figure 5C).
evidence: Figure 5C shows line profile quantification of cohesin intensity.

claim: The increase in axis-associated signal for SMC-3 in wapl-1 mutants is 59% compared with wild-type controls.
source: The average difference between axis-associated and inter-chromosomal signal for COH-3/4 was increased by 114% in wapl-1 mutants compared with wild-type controls, while the increase observed for REC-8 and SMC-3 was 27% and 59% respectively (Figure 5C).
evidence: Figure 5C shows line profile quantification of cohesin intensity.

claim: The intermediate increase of axis-associated SMC-3 levels is expected since SMC-3 should form part of both REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin complexes.
source: The intermediate increase of axis-associated SMC-3 levels is to be expected since SMC-3 should form part of both REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin complexes.
evidence: Logical inference based on known cohesin complex composition.

claim: The amount of COH-4 associated with DNA is increased in wapl-1 mutants compared to wild-type controls.
source: Separation of soluble and DNA-bound protein fractions from whole-worm extracts confirmed that the amount of COH-4 associated with DNA is increased in wapl-1 mutants compared to wild-type controls (Figure 5D–E and Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Figure 5D-E shows Western blot analysis of protein fractionation.

claim: In the absence of WAPL-1 there is a large increase in the amount of cohesin associated with axial elements, and most of this increase corresponds to cohesin complexes containing the COH-3/4 kleisins.

claim: RAD-51 foci are not observed in germ lines of wapl-1 spo-11 rec-8 triple mutants.

claim: Removing WAPL-1 from rec-8 syp-1 double mutants causes a large decrease of chromosome fragments and an increase in univalents.

Based on this analysis, chromosome fragments were defined by an area smaller than 120 pixels and 49% of chromatin bodies in syp-1 rec-8 oocytes fell within this category (Figure 6E). evidence: Figure 6E shows automated quantification of chromatin body sizes.

claim: 49% of chromatin bodies in syp-1 rec-8 oocytes are chromosome fragments.

claim: 25% of chromatin bodies in coh-4 rec-8 oocytes have an area corresponding to chromosome fragments.

In agreement with this, 25% of chromatin bodies in coh-4 rec-8 oocytes had an area corresponding to chromosome fragments, while this number was reduced to 8% in wapl-1 coh-4 rec-8 oocytes (Figure 6G–H).
evidence: Figure 6H shows quantification of chromatin body area sizes.

claim: 8% of chromatin bodies in wapl-1 coh-4 rec-8 oocytes have an area corresponding to chromosome fragments.

evidence: Figure 6H shows quantification of chromatin body area sizes.

claim: WAPL-1 antagonizes SCC mediated by COH-3/4 both in the presence and absence of SPO-11 DSBs.
source: These observations demonstrate that WAPL-1 antagonizes SCC mediated by COH-3/4 both in the presence and absence of SPO-11 DSBs.
evidence: Summary statement based on observations in multiple genetic backgrounds.

claim: Sister chromatids remain attached in the diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 mutants.
source: Sister chromatids remain attached in the diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 mutants, but the contact between them is often limited to a very small region, giving rec-8 univalents a bilobed appearance that contrasts with the rounded appearance of univalents observed in recombination-deficient mutants such as spo-11 (Figure 6A)(Severson et al., 2009; Collette et al., 2011).
evidence: Figure 6A shows morphology of diakinesis oocytes in rec-8 mutants.

claim: The contact between sister chromatids in rec-8 mutant oocytes is often limited to a very small region, giving rec-8 univalents a bilobed appearance.
source: Sister chromatids remain attached in the diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 mutants, but the contact between them is often limited to a very small region, giving rec-8 univalents a bilobed appearance that contrasts with the rounded appearance of univalents observed in recombination-deficient mutants such as spo-11 (Figure 6A)(Severson et al., 2009; Collette et al., 2011).
evidence: Visual observation of chromosome morphology in Figure 6A.

claim: Sister attachments in rec-8 oocytes require SPO-11 DSBs.
source: Why sisters are weakly attached in rec-8 oocytes remains unknown, but these attachments require SPO-11 DSBs (Severson et al., 2009), leading to the proposal that DSBs induce phosphorylation of COH-3/4, which in turn make these complexes cohesive in a pathway similar to the damage-induced cohesion observed in mitotic yeast cells (Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008; Severson and Meyer, 2014).
evidence: Citation of previous work showing DSB requirement.

claim: Oocytes from rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants display a dramatic increase in the number of DAPI-stained bodies (average 23.89) compared with rec-8 (average 13.06) and cosa-1 (average 11.83) single mutants.
source: To test this hypothesis we built worms lacking REC-8 and COSA-1, a protein required for the late stages of crossover formation but not for the induction of DSBs (Yokoo et al., 2012). Strikingly, oocytes from rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants display a dramatic increase in the number of DAPI-stained bodies (average 23.89) compared with rec-8 (average 13.06) and cosa-1 (average 11.83) single mutants, suggesting extensive separation of sister chromatids (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: Figure 7B shows quantification of DAPI-stained bodies in different genotypes.

claim: The dramatic increase in DAPI-stained bodies in rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants suggests extensive separation of sister chromatids.
source: Strikingly, oocytes from rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants display a dramatic increase in the number of DAPI-stained bodies (average 23.89) compared with rec-8 (average 13.06) and cosa-1 (average 11.83) single mutants, suggesting extensive separation of sister chromatids (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: High number of DAPI-stained bodies indicates separated sister chromatids.

claim: FISH experiments confirm extensive separation of sister chromatids in diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants.
source: FISH experiments confirmed extensive separation of sister chromatids in diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants, while also demonstrating that SCC is not affected in pachytene nuclei of these same mutants (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: Figure 7D shows FISH analysis with four 5S rDNA signals indicating separated sisters.

claim: SCC is not affected in pachytene nuclei of rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants.
source: FISH experiments confirmed extensive separation of sister chromatids in diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 cosa-1 double mutants, while also demonstrating that SCC is not affected in pachytene nuclei of these same mutants (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: Figure 7C shows FISH analysis with two 5S rDNA signals in pachytene indicating intact cohesion.

claim: Loss of cohesion in rec-8 cosa-1 mutants must occur during the chromosome remodeling process that starts at late pachytene.
source: Thus, loss of cohesion must occur during the chromosome remodeling process that starts at late pachytene.
evidence: Inference from cohesion being intact in pachytene but lost in diakinesis.

claim: Attachments between sister chromatids in diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 mutants require the presence of a recombination event formed by the COSA-1-dependent crossover pathway.
source: These results suggest that attachments between sister chromatids in diakinesis oocytes of rec-8 mutants require the presence of a recombination event formed by the COSA-1-dependent crossover pathway.
evidence: Inference from loss of cohesion when COSA-1 is removed from rec-8 mutants.

claim: Removing WAPL-1 from rec-8 cosa-1 mutants restores cohesion in diakinesis oocytes.

claim: WAPL-1 antagonizes cohesion mediated by COH-3/4 during late prophase.

claim: The soluble pool of SMC-1 that starts accumulating at late pachytene persists during diakinesis in wild-type worms.
source: Imaging of germ lines from wild-type worms expressing SMC-1::GFP demonstrated that the soluble pool of SMC-1 that starts accumulating at late pachytene persists during diakinesis, and that the oocyte about to be ovulated (-1 oocyte) displayed a reduction in the intensity of chromosome-associated cohesin compared to the -2 oocyte of the same germ line (Figure 8A).
evidence: Figure 8A shows SMC-1::GFP staining in diakinesis oocytes.

claim: The -1 oocyte displays a reduction in the intensity of chromosome-associated cohesin compared to the -2 oocyte in wild-type germ lines.
source: Imaging of germ lines from wild-type worms expressing SMC-1::GFP demonstrated that the soluble pool of SMC-1 that starts accumulating at late pachytene persists during diakinesis, and that the oocyte about to be ovulated (-1 oocyte) displayed a reduction in the intensity of chromosome-associated cohesin compared to the -2 oocyte of the same germ line (Figure 8A).
evidence: Figure 8A shows comparison of SMC-1::GFP intensity between -1 and -2 oocytes.

claim: A clear reduction in chromosome-associated cohesin occurs in late diakinesis oocytes of wapl-1 mutant germ lines.
source: Since Wapl is required for the prophase pathway that removes cohesin before metaphase in mitotic cells (Haarhuis et al., 2014) and a similar pathway operates during meiosis in plants (De et al., 2014), we tested whether WAPL-1 is required for cohesin removal in late diakinesis oocytes. Surprisingly, a clear reduction in chromosome-associated cohesin occurs in late diakinesis oocytes of wapl-1 mutant germ lines (Figure 8A).
evidence: Figure 8A shows reduction in SMC-1::GFP intensity in late diakinesis oocytes of wapl-1 mutants.

claim: In most cases (21 out of 26 analyzed germ lines) the reduction in chromosome-associated cohesin is evident between the -2 and -1 oocytes in wapl-1 mutants.

evidence: Figure 8A shows comparison of soluble SMC-1::GFP between WT and wapl-1 mutants.

claim: A reduction in chromosome bound SMC-1::GFP occurs in late diakinesis oocytes of both wild-type and wapl-1 mutant germ lines as observed by super resolution structural illumination microscopy.

These experiments also demonstrated that a reduction in chromosome bound SMC-1::GFP occurs in late diakinesis oocytes of both wild-type and wapl-1 mutant germ lines (Figure 8B).
evidence: Figure 8B shows super resolution images of SMC-1::GFP in diakinesis oocytes.

source: Our study reveals that WAPL-1 antagonizes stable cohesin binding throughout meiotic prophase, affecting the morphogenesis of axial elements at the onset of meiotic prophase, the higher-order structure of chromosomes during pachytene, the process of chromosome remodeling during diplotene, and cohesion in diakinesis oocytes.

claim: WAPL-1 affects meiotic prophase events by promoting cohesin removal from the beginning of meiosis, not just as part of a meiotic prophase pathway that removes cohesin during late stages of chromosome condensation.

evidence: Summary statement based on observations of WAPL-1 effects throughout meiotic prophase.

claim: The cohesin complex mediates sister chromatid cohesion between S-phase and chromosome segregation at anaphase.
source: The cohesin complex, which mediates sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) between S-phase and chromosome segregation at anaphase (Michaelis et al., 1997), consists of two SMC proteins (Smc1 and Smc3) plus a kleisin subunit (Scc1/Rad21), forming a tripartite structure that topologically embraces DNA molecules (Haering et al., 2002; Haering et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge about cohesin function with citations.
